# DevPulse

> DevPulse (Devpulse Limited) is a UK studio that builds iOS and Android apps for clients and publishes its own apps and games. This file summarises the site for AI agents and language models.

AuthSome is a free authenticator app made by DevPulse. It makes the short codes that websites and apps ask for after your password when you sign in, and it makes them on the device. This is two factor authentication, also called 2FA or two step verification. These are time based one time codes, known as TOTP. AuthSome keeps personal and work Accounts apart in Profiles. An Account is one service the user has added, such as Google or GitHub.

- Price: free. No ads, no subscription, no purchases and no sign up.
- Platforms: iPhone with iOS 26 or later, iPad with iPadOS 26 or later and Mac with macOS 26 or later. One app for all three. There is no Android or Apple Watch version.
- Status: coming soon to the App Store. It is not available to download yet.
- Profiles: each Profile, such as Personal or Work, holds its own Accounts, and the user sees only the Profile they are in. Inside a Profile, Accounts can be sorted into Folders.
- AutoFill: AuthSome suggests the 2FA code above the keyboard when a sign in page asks for one. The user confirms with Face ID or Touch ID.
- Backup and sync: Accounts are backed up to the private iCloud of the user and appear on their other devices, so a new device signed in to the same Apple Account already has them. Everything the user adds is end to end encrypted, including Secrets and recovery codes. Apple cannot read it and neither can DevPulse.
- Import and export: imports from Google Authenticator, 2FAS, Aegis, a text file of otpauth setup links and AuthSome backups. Accounts can be exported to a file protected with a password.
- Security: the app is locked, and the user unlocks it with Face ID, Touch ID or the device passcode, or the login password on a Mac. Secrets, the keys that 2FA codes are made from, are kept in the device Keychain.
- Recovery codes: the backup codes a service hands out can be kept with its Account. Viewing them needs Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode each time.
- Mac menu bar: on a Mac, a menu bar panel lists the Accounts with their 2FA codes, and a click copies one.
- Privacy: AuthSome collects nothing. It has no servers of its own, no tracking and no code from other companies.
- Languages: 44.
- Maker: DevPulse, United Kingdom.
- Contact: support@devpulse.co.uk

The service names and logos shown on the AuthSome page are examples. AuthSome is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any of them.

## Apps

- [AuthSome](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/): A free authenticator app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that makes 2FA codes. Coming soon to the App Store. Its facts are above.
- [Kids Paint](https://devpulse.co.uk/kidspaint/): A drawing and colouring app for kids on iPhone, iPad and Android.
- [TwinFin](https://devpulse.co.uk/twinfin/): A one thumb arcade game for iPhone with a new level every day.
- [Coconut Rocket](https://devpulse.co.uk/coconut-rocket/): An endless arcade climber for iPhone.
- [All apps](https://devpulse.co.uk/apps/): Every DevPulse app, including the free Mac utilities FannyBoost and ScreenBoost.

## AuthSome

- [AuthSome home](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/): what the app is and what it does.
- [Privacy policy](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/privacy/): what stays on the device, what goes to iCloud, and what is not collected.
- [Support](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/support/): what the app does, what it costs and which devices it works on, then how to add Accounts, use a 2FA code, set up AutoFill, import from another app, back up and move to a new device.

## AuthSome Guides

Plain guides to 2FA codes and authenticator apps on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Facts about other apps come from the pages of their makers, which each guide lists.

- [All guides](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/)
- [How to Export Google Authenticator to Another App on iPhone](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/export-google-authenticator-to-another-app/): Tap Menu, Transfer accounts, Export accounts, scan the QR code in the new app, and check before you delete.
- [Do Authenticator Apps Transfer to a New iPhone?](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/do-authenticator-apps-transfer-to-new-iphone/): It depends on the app. What each maker says, what to turn on first, and a safe order for switching.
- [How to Move 2FA Codes From Android to iPhone](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/move-2fa-codes-from-android-to-iphone/): It depends on your Android app. The route for Google Authenticator, Aegis, 2FAS and Microsoft Authenticator.
- [Authy Desktop Is Gone. What to Use on a Mac Instead](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/authy-desktop-alternative-mac/): Authy Desktop ended in March 2024. Which Mac apps replace it, and how to move when Authy has no export.
- [Can You Use an Authenticator App on a Mac?](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/authenticator-app-on-mac/): Yes. Use the Passwords app from Apple, or a separate authenticator app that has a Mac version.
- [Can You Use the Same Authenticator App on Two Devices?](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/authenticator-app-on-two-devices/): Yes. Use an app that syncs, or scan the same QR code on both devices when you set up 2FA.
- [Which Authenticator Apps Are Free With No Ads or Subscription?](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/free-authenticator-app-no-ads/): 2FAS and Proton say they have no ads. Which apps are free, and how to spot one that charges weekly.
- [How to AutoFill 2FA Codes From an Authenticator App on iPhone](https://devpulse.co.uk/authsome/guides/autofill-2fa-codes-iphone/): Turn it on in Settings, General, AutoFill & Passwords. Which apps say they fill 2FA codes.
